summary: picasso-plugin-q ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is variable-name obfuscated, detects platform/arch (including musl via /etc/os-release), downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases into a temp directory, unzips it, marks the binary executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with string-array rotation and hex-encoded identifiers, unreadable to normal review. The legitimate qlik-oss picasso-plugin-q ships neither a preinstall hook nor a math_init.js bundle, and the Qlik/picasso plugin's advertised purpose has no need for the Bun runtime. Installing the package auto-executes attacker-supplied obfuscated code on the installer's host under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime that bypasses Node-based scanning.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
